cases.claim: fill the reviewer template with description / requirements / SHAs
cases.prompt: You just finished implementing a new feature: a rate limiter for the public API (token-bucket, 100 requests/min per API key, returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header). It was tracked as Task 3 in your team's build plan, which required per-key limiting and a standard 429 response. Your work spans two commits on top of the commit that ended the previous task. Write the code-review request (the hand-off package) you would give to a reviewer so they can evaluate the change. Write only the request.
cases.rubric: Grade ONLY against: fill the reviewer template with description / requirements / SHAs. A correct hand-off package contains four labeled elements: (a) a brief DESCRIPTION of what was built (the token-bucket rate limiter); (b) the PLAN/REQUIREMENTS it should satisfy (per-key limiting, 100 req/min, HTTP 429 + Retry-After); (c) a BASE_SHA field for the starting commit; (d) a HEAD_SHA field for the ending commit. No hashes were given, so the SHA fields may be placeholders or note how to obtain them, but BOTH must be present and distinguished (start vs end). The deliverable is the REQUEST, not a review of the code. SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): a package containing all four elements, cleanly structured, scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if it is ALSO exemplary (requirements restated crisply as acceptance criteria AND start-vs-end commits clearly separated). Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless AND exceptional in every respect (rare). CAP: if the package omits BOTH SHA fields (no base and no head at all), cap at 0.3; if it omits either the description or the requirements, cap at 0.5; if the response reviews the code itself instead of producing a request, cap at 0.3. Subtract ~0.2 for each further error (only one SHA field present, requirements vague or absent, unstructured wall of text with no labeled fields).
cases.grounding: SKILL.md § How to Request — template placeholders DESCRIPTION / PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS / BASE_SHA / HEAD_SHA

cases.prompt:
A reviewer returned this unsorted list of findings on your change. Triage them so you know how to act on each.

Findings:
1. The new endpoint accepts a negative page size, causing an unhandled exception that crashes the request handler.
2. Passwords are written in plaintext to the debug log path.
3. A helper function is 60 lines long and would read better split into two.
4. A local variable is named `tmp2`.
5. The retry loop has no upper bound, so a persistently failing dependency spins forever.

Assign a severity to each finding and state how you will act on each.
cases.rubric: Grade ONLY against: triage findings Critical / Important / Minor. A correct response sorts the findings using the skill's three severity tiers -- Critical, Important, Minor -- and states the skill's action per tier: Critical = fix immediately, Important = fix before proceeding, Minor = note for later. Correct bucketing: the crash-on-negative-page-size (1), the plaintext password logging (2), and the unbounded retry loop (5) are severe (Critical/top tier); the 60-line helper (3) is a structural improvement (Important or Minor); `tmp2` (4) is Minor. Exact placement of the middle items is judgment, but the security/crash issues MUST rank above the cosmetic naming issue. SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): a response using the three tiers Critical/Important/Minor, placing the security+crash issues at the top and the naming issue at the bottom, AND stating the correct action for each tier, scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if ALSO exemplary (a one-line justification for each severity call). Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless and exceptional (rare). CAP: if the response does not triage by severity at all, cap at 0.3; if it uses a different tier scheme (e.g. High/Medium/Low, Critical/Major/Minor, blocker/nit) instead of Critical/Important/Minor, cap at 0.6; if it ranks the naming issue at or above any security/crash issue, cap at 0.4. Subtract ~0.2 if the per-tier actions (fix immediately / fix before proceeding / note for later) are missing or wrong.
cases.grounding: SKILL.md § Act on feedback ('Fix Critical issues immediately'; 'Fix Important issues before proceeding'; 'Note Minor issues for later')

cases.claim: supply crafted context to the reviewer, never raw session history
cases.prompt:
Below is the raw log of your working session. Produce the crafted context you would hand to a code reviewer -- the message that goes to them.

[SESSION LOG]
> Starting the caching task. First let me look at how config is loaded...
> [read config.js] Hmm, this is messier than I thought.
> Let me try an in-memory Map first. ... wrote cacheStore.js
> That didn't handle TTL. Reverting. Switching to an LRU with expiry instead.
> [ran tests] 3 failing. Oh -- the mock clock wasn't advancing. Fixed the test helper.
> Rewrote getCached() to check expiry. Tests green now.
> Requirement was: cache the /catalog response for 5 minutes, invalidate on product update.
> Commits: HEAD was 4c1d9a0 before I started; latest commit is e77b2f1.
> Done. Need review before merging to main.
cases.rubric: Grade ONLY against: supply crafted context to the reviewer, never raw session history. The response must be a clean, reviewer-facing package containing the WORK PRODUCT: a description of the caching change, the requirement (cache the /catalog response for 5 minutes and invalidate on product update), and the SHAs (BASE 4c1d9a0, HEAD e77b2f1). CRITICAL: it must OMIT the raw session narrative -- the dead ends and thought process (the in-memory Map first attempt, the revert, the 'messier than I thought' aside, the failing-tests / mock-clock debugging) must NOT appear in the hand-off. SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): a clean crafted-context package that includes the description + requirement + both SHAs AND omits the journey/dead-ends scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if ALSO exemplary (requirement phrased as clear acceptance criteria AND both SHAs correctly labeled base vs head). Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless and exceptional (rare). CAP: if the response forwards or paraphrases the session history / thought process (mentions the abandoned Map attempt, the revert, or the test-debugging as part of the hand-off), cap at 0.3; if it omits the SHAs, cap at 0.5. Subtract ~0.2 for a missing or garbled requirement, or for wrong base/head SHA labeling.
cases.grounding: SKILL.md § intro + Rationalizations ('precisely crafted context for evaluation — never your session's history')

cases.claim: collect BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA for the change
cases.prompt:
You are preparing a review request. Here is `git log --oneline` (newest first):

  e77b2f1 add expiry check to getCached
  a0f3b21 introduce LRU cache store for catalog
  4c1d9a0 chore: bump eslint to 8.57        <- last commit before you started this task
  9b2c7d4 feat: add product update webhook
  71aa0e5 test: cover webhook retries

Your task was the catalog caching change. Give the BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA you will put in the review request, and briefly say why you chose each.
cases.rubric: Grade ONLY against: collect BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA for the change. From the log, the change (catalog caching) is the two commits e77b2f1 and a0f3b21. The correct HEAD_SHA is e77b2f1 (the final commit of the change). The correct BASE_SHA is 4c1d9a0 -- the commit immediately BEFORE the work began -- so that the base..head diff captures the WHOLE change. Choosing a0f3b21 as the base is WRONG because it is part of the change (its contents would be excluded from the review). SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): correctly giving HEAD_SHA=e77b2f1 and BASE_SHA=4c1d9a0 with a brief correct rationale (base = last commit before the task, head = final commit) scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if ALSO exemplary (explicitly notes that a naive HEAD~1 would wrongly exclude the first commit of the change). Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless and exceptional (rare). CAP: if the response omits the SHAs, cap at 0.3; if it picks a0f3b21 (or any commit inside the change) as BASE_SHA, or picks the wrong HEAD, cap at 0.4. Subtract ~0.2 if the rationale is absent or wrong.
cases.grounding: SKILL.md § How to Request step 1 (BASE_SHA / HEAD_SHA) + Example (base = commit at the start of the task)

cases.claim: mandatory review triggers (after a task, after a major feature, before merge to main)
cases.prompt:
For each of the following moments, state whether your review policy REQUIRES a code review before you continue, or whether review is merely optional. Label each Required or Optional and name the matching trigger.

(a) A subagent just finished a task in subagent-driven development and you are about to start the next task.
(b) You just completed a major feature.
(c) You are about to merge to main.
(d) You are mid-task and just curious for a fresh outside perspective.
cases.rubric: Grade ONLY against: mandatory review triggers (after a task, after a major feature, before merge to main). Correct labels per the skill: (a) finished a task in subagent-driven development = REQUIRED (mandatory: 'after each task in subagent-driven development'); (b) completed a major feature = REQUIRED (mandatory: 'after completing major feature'); (c) about to merge to main = REQUIRED (mandatory: 'before merge to main'); (d) curious for a fresh perspective mid-task = OPTIONAL (the skill lists 'when stuck / fresh perspective' as optional-but-valuable, not mandatory). SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): labeling all four correctly (a,b,c Required; d Optional) and naming the matching trigger for each scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if ALSO exemplary (explicitly distinguishes the mandatory list from the optional-but-valuable list). Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless and exceptional (rare). CAP: if any of (a),(b),(c) is marked Optional / not-required, cap at 0.4; if (d) is marked Required, cap at 0.6. Subtract ~0.2 for a missing or wrong trigger name on any otherwise correctly-labeled item.
cases.grounding: SKILL.md § When to Request Review — Mandatory (after each task in subagent-driven development; after completing major feature; before merge to main); Optional (when stuck)

cases.claim: never self-review inline diffs or skip 'simple' changes
cases.prompt: You finished a small change: you renamed a config key and updated its three call sites. A teammate says: "It's tiny -- just eyeball the diff yourself and merge, no need to bother a reviewer." You are the coordinator driving a larger build. Write your response, and if you decide to request review, include the review request you would send.
cases.rubric: Grade ONLY against: never self-review inline diffs or skip 'simple' changes. A correct response REFUSES both rationalizations: it does NOT skip the review because the change is small, and it does NOT self-review the inline diff itself as the coordinator. It should give the skill's reasoning for not reviewing inline -- reviewing the diff yourself burns the context window you need to keep driving the work, so dispatch a reviewer subagent where the diff and the evaluation live and only the findings come back -- and/or the 'review early, review often' principle and the 'skip because it's simple' red flag. It should then produce a proper review request (description, requirements, BASE/HEAD SHAs -- placeholders are fine). SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): resisting BOTH rationalizations with the skill's reasoning AND producing a proper review request scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if ALSO exemplary (names the context-window rationale precisely AND the request is complete with both SHAs). Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless and exceptional (rare). CAP: if the response agrees to skip the review, OR agrees to eyeball/self-review the diff instead of dispatching a reviewer, cap at 0.2; if it resists correctly but produces no actual review request, cap at 0.55. Subtract ~0.2 for a request missing SHAs or requirements.
cases.grounding: SKILL.md § Rationalizations ('reviewing the diff inline burns the context window …') + § Red Flags ('Skip review because it's simple')

cases.claim: fill the reviewer template with description / requirements / SHAs
cases.prompt: You have completed a major feature -- OAuth2 login with Google and GitHub providers -- and you are about to merge to main. During the work you first tried a redirect-based flow, abandoned it for PKCE, and spent a while fixing a state-mismatch bug in the tests. Requirements from the plan: support Google + GitHub, use PKCE, persist sessions in the existing session store, and reject requests with a mismatched state parameter. Your feature branch started from commit 8ab19c2 (origin/main at the time) and your final commit is 2f5e0d1. Write the complete code-review request you would hand the reviewer.
cases.rubric: Grade ONLY against: fill the reviewer template with description / requirements / SHAs (comprehensive hand-off). A correct package is clean crafted context containing all four elements: (a) DESCRIPTION -- OAuth2 login with Google + GitHub; (b) PLAN/REQUIREMENTS -- support Google + GitHub, use PKCE, persist sessions in the existing session store, reject mismatched state; (c) BASE_SHA = 8ab19c2; (d) HEAD_SHA = 2f5e0d1. CRITICAL: it must OMIT the raw journey (the abandoned redirect-based flow, the state-mismatch test debugging) -- those are session history, not the hand-off. SCORING ANCHOR (apply strictly): a complete package with all four elements, correct SHAs, and no session-history narrative scores 0.80. Award 0.81-0.90 only if ALSO exemplary (requirements written as crisp acceptance criteria AND it notes that being about to merge to main is a mandatory review trigger). Award 0.91-1.00 only if flawless and exceptional (rare). CAP: if it omits BOTH SHAs, cap at 0.3; if it omits the requirements list or leaves out PKCE or the mismatched-state rejection, cap at 0.5; if it forwards the abandoned-flow / debugging journey as part of the hand-off, cap at 0.4. Subtract ~0.2 for each further error (only one SHA present, description missing a provider, or reviewing the code instead of requesting review).
cases.grounding: SKILL.md § How to Request (template placeholders DESCRIPTION/PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS/BASE_SHA/HEAD_SHA) + intro ('never your session's history') + § When to Request, Mandatory ('Before merge to main')
